countries.name: India
countries.summary: India's higher-education system is overseen by the Ministry of Education and its statutory regulators - the University Grants Commission for universities and degrees, the All India Council for Technical Education for technical and management programmes, and the National Medical Commission for medical education. International applicants normally enter through an institution's own international-admissions office, through the government's Study in India portal, or through a centrally administered scheme such as DASA for engineering and architecture seats at NITs, IIITs and other centrally funded technical institutes. Entry rules differ by nationality, residency status, the prior qualification held and the discipline chosen.
countries.whyStudentsChooseIt: International applicants look at India for English-taught degrees across computing, engineering, management, design, sciences, law and health disciplines, and for a single national application route: the Ministry of Education's Study in India portal issues an SII ID and lets an applicant send one profile to several participating institutes. Government-funded study places also exist through Indian Council for Cultural Relations scholarship schemes, which are applied for through Indian diplomatic missions rather than directly to a university. What an individual applicant can access depends on citizenship, residency status, how the prior qualification is assessed for equivalence, and whether the programme is attached to a national entrance test.
countries.climate: Climate varies widely by region, from alpine Himalayan conditions in the north to tropical coastal and semi-arid zones further south, with a June-to-September monsoon across most of the country.
countries.metaTitle: Study in India: Guide for International Students
countries.metaDescription: Regulators, admission routes, entrance tests, student visa and FRRO rules that international applicants should verify before applying to an Indian university.

The curriculum covers social work theory and methods, sociology, psychology, social policy, human rights, community organisation and research, with supervised fieldwork placements in agencies, hospitals or community organisations throughout the course. Programmes usually last three or four years. Graduates work in NGOs, public welfare services and healthcare, or continue to a master's in social work; some countries also require registration to practise.

Core study covers accounting, finance, marketing, organisational behaviour, human resource management, operations, business law and economics, usually followed by a specialisation such as business analytics, international business, digital marketing, finance or healthcare management, plus an internship or live project. Programmes run for three years in many systems and four years where an honours or research year is added. Graduates move into entry-level management roles or continue to an MBA or a specialist master's degree.

The LPU version combines conceptual foundation coursework with intensive studio practice in interior and furniture design, adds design research methods and a dissertation, and allows an interdisciplinary minor. The degree builds a broad base in laboratory work, mathematics and scientific method and usually lasts three years, or four with an honours or research year. Students learn surveying, building materials and construction, structural mechanics, concrete technology, soil mechanics, hydraulics, estimating and costing, and technical drawing, with workshop practice and site training. In many systems it takes about three years after lower-secondary school or less after upper-secondary school, and it can allow lateral entry into the second year of a civil-engineering degree. Graduates work as site supervisors, draughtspersons and junior engineers.

The diploma typically lasts about three years after lower-secondary school and can allow lateral entry into a mechanical-engineering degree. Graduates work in production, maintenance and quality roles.

The syllabus covers constitutional law, contract, torts, criminal law, property, corporate law, procedure and jurisprudence, with moot courts, legal aid clinics and internships. Programmes must be recognised by the Bar Council of India for graduates to seek enrolment as advocates in India.

universities.name: Jamia Millia Islamia
universities.summary: Jamia Millia Islamia (JMI) is a public Central University in New Delhi. Founded in 1920 at Aligarh, it moved to Delhi in 1925 and became a Central University by Act of Parliament in 1988. Its 239-acre Jamia Nagar campus teaches sciences, engineering, law, architecture, management, education, the arts and dentistry, and admits foreign nationals to supernumerary seats.
universities.campusLifestyle: JMI's campus in Jamia Nagar, south Delhi, covers 239 acres and is partly residential. The prospectus reports over 20,000 students, about 68% from outside Delhi, and roughly 3% from abroad representing more than 30 countries. The library system, led by the Dr. Zakir Husain central library, holds over 6 lakh books, 6,000 rare books and 2,243 manuscripts. The sports complex has an air-conditioned indoor stadium, a cricket ground used for Ranji Trophy matches, and courts for tennis, basketball and volleyball.
universities.cityProfile: JMI sits on Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Marg in Jamia Nagar, New Delhi 110025, and runs a single main campus there. Foreign students deal with the Foreign Students' Advisor (FSA) in Rooms 20-21, Old SRK Hostel, Gate No. 8. Every foreign student on a student visa valid for more than 180 days must register with the FRRO within 14 days of first arrival, using a bonafide certificate and an FSIS ID generated from Form-S at the FSA office. JMI asks foreign students to arrive with enough money to cover living costs in Delhi, and warns ICCR scholars that stipends can take a few months to start. Fees are paid in rupees at the dollar equivalent, because JMI does not accept dollar notes or cheques; two nationalised banks operate in the campus area for opening an account. JMI says it has not authorised any agency or individual to act on its behalf for admissions.
universities.practicalExposure: The National Board of Accreditation lists five JMI B.Tech branches on its Tier I (Washington Accord) register until 30 June 2028: Civil, Computer, Electrical, Electronics & Communication and Mechanical Engineering. NIRF 2025 ranks JMI 5th in Architecture, 8th in Law, 24th in Engineering and 28th in Management. Research runs through more than thirty centres, including the Centre for Nanoscience & Nanotechnology, the Centre for Interdisciplinary Research in Basic Sciences, the Multidisciplinary Centre for Advanced Research and Studies and the Centre for Theoretical Physics. JMI's prospectus reports 67 research projects with grants of over INR 33 crore, 41 patents filed in 2024-25 and a cumulative Scopus h-index of 212. Skills-based B.Voc. degrees in medical laboratory sciences, molecular diagnostics and medical electrophysiology are run by DDU Kaushal Kendra, and the M.Tech programmes give admission preference to GATE-qualified Indian applicants while foreign nationals use the supernumerary route.
universities.hostelOverview: JMI says hostel space for foreign students is very limited and not guaranteed; about 30% of all students get a place. The International Boys Hostel gives preference to Ph.D. and postgraduate students and has no mess. Its FSA fee sheet lists INR 5,050 at admission, including a refundable INR 3,000 caution deposit, plus INR 5,700 a month for an air-conditioned room or INR 4,000 for a non-AC room, covering rent, electricity and water, maintenance and a cultural fee. Women apply to the Provost (Girls). Every hostel resident must file Form C with the FSA office.
universities.dietarySupport: The International Boys Hostel has no mess, so residents arrange their own meals; JMI's FSA sheet lists no meal plan for foreign students. Mess arrangements in other halls are set by the Provost (Boys) and Provost (Girls) offices under the Hostel Bye-Laws, which are available from those offices.
universities.safetyOverview: JMI runs a zero-tolerance anti-ragging policy, and ragging leads to expulsion. The Ansari Health Centre gives students free primary care, with doctors until 10 pm including weekends, a 24-hour ambulance and visiting specialists twice a week. JMI advises foreign students to buy medical insurance of INR 5 lakh (about US$6,700) a year.
universities.studentSupport: The Foreign Students' Advisor (fsa@jmi.ac.in, +91-11-26981717 ext. 1760) handles admission, Form-S and the FSIS ID for FRRO registration, and every foreign student fills a registration form there on joining. Selected applicants can collect the provisional admission letter in person or receive it by email.

faq.question: Is Jamia Millia Islamia a public or private university?
faq.answer: JMI is a public Central University funded by the Government of India. It began in 1920 at Aligarh, moved to Delhi in 1925 and became a Central University by an Act of Parliament in 1988. UGC lists it among India's 56 Central Universities.

faq.question: How do international students apply to JMI?
faq.answer: Foreign passport holders apply online at admission.jmi.ac.in under the supernumerary foreign-national category, paying an application fee equivalent to INR 1,000 for each programme. The Foreign Students' Advisor (FSA) handles these applications. ICCR scholarship nominees apply through ICCR's A2A portal, and JMI also accepts applications through the Study in India programme.

faq.question: Do foreign students have to take JMI's entrance test?
faq.answer: No, for most programmes. The 25% supernumerary seats are for foreign students who meet a programme's eligibility but do not sit the entrance test, and JMI ranks them on marks in their last qualifying examination. The B.P.T. is the exception: foreign nationals must appear in NEET-UG. Foreign students may also sit the entrance test and compete for regular seats under the general category.

faq.question: What are the eligibility requirements for foreign students?
faq.answer: JMI applies the same minimum eligibility to foreign students as to Indian students, programme by programme, as set out in its prospectus. For example, B.Tech needs Class 12 with at least 55% in Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics, and the MBA needs a bachelor's degree with 50%. The school board or university must be on the AIU list, or the applicant needs an AIU or UGC equivalence certificate.

faq.question: How much does JMI cost for international students?
faq.answer: Tuition is set in US dollars per semester by faculty and home region. Most nationalities pay US$1,800 a semester in engineering, law, management and architecture PG, US$1,500 in the sciences and US$1,200 in the social sciences; SAARC, West Asian and African students pay less. Add an INR 2,000 admission fee, an INR 8,000 refundable deposit, housing and insurance of about US$6,700 cover a year.

faq.question: What language are JMI programmes taught in?
faq.answer: JMI's Ordinance 11 makes Urdu the default medium, allows English and Hindi where the Academic Council approves, and requires English for science, technical and professional courses. The programmes listed on this page are taught in English; for humanities and language programmes, confirm the teaching language with the department before applying.

faq.question: Is an English test such as IELTS or TOEFL required?
faq.answer: JMI's foreign-student guidelines set no IELTS or TOEFL minimum for undergraduate or master's admission; TOEFL or IELTS is listed only as a preference for Ph.D. applicants. Applicants still need attested English translations of every transcript not issued in English.

faq.question: When is the intake and what are the deadlines?
faq.answer: JMI admits once a year for a session that starts in mid-July. For 2026-27 the FSA deadlines were 25 May 2026 for undergraduate and 30 May 2026 for postgraduate applications, with results due by 15 June and 17 July respectively. Admission formalities closed on 31 July (UG) and 31 August (PG). The 2027-28 schedule is published on the FSA page.

faq.question: Which visa do I need and what happens after arrival?
faq.answer: Undergraduate, postgraduate and diploma students need an Indian Student (S-1) visa, preferably endorsed to Jamia Millia Islamia; tourist, medical, X and short-term visas are not accepted. Show the visa to the FSA office within one month of admission. Students with visas over 180 days register with the FRRO within 14 days of arrival, using the FSIS ID from Form-S.

faq.question: Is JMI accredited and ranked?
faq.answer: Yes. NAAC accredited JMI with an A++ grade (CGPA 3.61) in its second cycle, declared in December 2021. NIRF 2025 ranks it 4th among universities, 13th overall, 5th in Architecture and 8th in Law. Five B.Tech branches are on NBA's Tier I (Washington Accord) register until 30 June 2028.

faq.question: Does JMI provide hostel accommodation for foreign students?
faq.answer: Places are very limited and not guaranteed. The International Boys Hostel prefers Ph.D. and PG students, has no mess and charges INR 5,700 a month for an air-conditioned room or INR 4,000 non-AC, plus INR 5,050 at admission. Women apply through the Provost (Girls).

faq.question: Are scholarships available for international students at JMI?
faq.answer: JMI reserves 5% of seats for students on Government of India scholarships through the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR). These are competitive and applied for through ICCR's A2A portal or the nearest Indian mission; ICCR scholars pay fees at the rate for Indian students. JMI does not publish its own fee waiver for supernumerary foreign-national seats.

faq.question: Can I get a refund if I cancel my admission?
faq.answer: If a supernumerary or self-financed admission is cancelled within a month, JMI refunds 80% of the fee in rupees, provided the refund is claimed within a year. After that only the security deposit is refunded or adjusted. Unclaimed credit balances are moved to JMI's scholarship fund after one year.

restrictions: Only foreign passport holders count as international students; NRI wards apply under a separate 5% quota with different rules

admissionsContent.overview: The two-year M.Tech. Environmental Health Risk & Safety Management (Self-Financed) is taught in English at the Department of Environmental Science, JMI's New Delhi campus. Foreign nationals compete for 6 supernumerary foreign-national seats on the merit of their qualifying-examination marks, without JMI's entrance test, applying through the Foreign Students' Advisor (FSA).

eligibility.intro: Entry needs an environmental M.Sc. or a relevant engineering bachelor's with at least 60% or a 6.75/10 grade.
items: M.Sc. (Environmental Science), M.Sc. (Environmental Science & Management) or equivalent
Or a bachelor's in Civil, Mechanical, Chemical, Electrical, Metallurgical, Mining or Agricultural Engineering, or another relevant engineering degree
At least 60% in an absolute system or a grade of 6.75 on a 10-point scale
The school or university must be on the AIU list, or an AIU/UGC equivalence certificate is needed
A valid foreign passport is required; JMI defines an international student as a foreign passport holder

applicationSteps: Apply online at admission.jmi.ac.in under the foreign-national supernumerary category and pay the non-refundable application fee equivalent to INR 1,000; each programme needs its own form and fee
Upload self-attested Class 10 and 12 and bachelor's marksheets with a grade-to-percentage conversion certificate, proof of age and your passport, with attested English translations
Email the qualifying-examination result to fsa@jmi.ac.in by the FSA deadline if it was still awaited when you applied
Check the provisional selection list, which JMI prepares on qualifying-examination merit, and collect or receive the provisional admission letter from the FSA office
Apply for an Indian Student (S-1) visa with the provisional admission letter, preferably endorsed in the name of Jamia Millia Islamia
Complete admission formalities: pay the first-semester fee in rupees plus the INR 2,000 admission fee and INR 8,000 security deposit, and submit the parent's financial-support affidavit
Within 14 days of arrival, register with the FRRO using the bonafide certificate and the FSIS ID generated from Form-S at the FSA office

academic: Class 10 and Class 12 marksheets or transcripts and the bachelor's degree marksheets, self-attested
Certificate converting grades or GPA into percentages
English translations attested by an authorised government agency
AIU or UGC equivalence certificate if the board or university is not on the AIU list
application: Valid passport (and visa, if already issued)
Proof of age
Affidavit on Rs 10 stamp paper from a parent for financial support (at final admission)
Gap-year affidavit from a notary, if there was a break in study
Online anti-ragging undertaking from the student and parent at antiragging.in

evidence.claimText: The University Grants Commission is the statutory body of the Government of India for coordination, determination and maintenance of standards of higher education, operating under the Ministry of Education.
evidence.sourceLabel: University Grants Commission (UGC) - official site
evidence.internalNotes: UGC publishes the authoritative lists of Central, State, Deemed-to-be and State Private universities, plus a published list of fake universities. Corroborated by the Study in India portal Indian Higher Education page, which states all institutions are governed by the Ministry of Education.

evidence.claimText: The All India Council for Technical Education is the Government of India statutory body for technical education, covering engineering, management and allied technical programmes.
evidence.sourceLabel: All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) - official site

evidence.claimText: The National Medical Commission is the Government of India regulator for medical education and medical institutions; medical and dental admission is governed separately from general higher education.
evidence.sourceLabel: National Medical Commission (NMC) - official site

evidence.claimText: India's higher-education landscape includes over 1,100 universities and more than 45,000 colleges, all governed by the Ministry of Education, and higher education begins after 12 years of schooling.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - Indian Higher Education
evidence.internalNotes: Portal-published counts are approximate and shift between AISHE cycles; treat them as indicative and re-check at review. Regulator identity is separately verified against UGC and AICTE.

evidence.claimText: The Study in India portal is the Government of India route for international applicants: the applicant registers for a compulsory SII ID, explores participating institutes and courses, submits applications to several institutes from one profile, accepts an offer letter, then applies for a student visa or student e-visa.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - official portal

evidence.claimText: The Bureau of Immigration directs foreign nationals who wish to apply to Indian institutes to register under the Study in India scheme, confirming the portal as a government-recognised route rather than a third-party service.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India

evidence.claimText: The Indian Council for Cultural Relations administers Government of India scholarship schemes for international students at UG, PG and PhD level, including AYUSH streams; applications are handled through the ICCR A2A scholarship portal and the applicant's Indian diplomatic mission.
evidence.sourceLabel: ICCR Admissions to Alumni (A2A) Scholarship Portal
evidence.internalNotes: Portal states that applicants should contact the Indian Mission for scholarship updates - eligibility and open cycles are mission-specific and vary by country, so no scheme may be presented as open to all nationalities.

evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals must obtain a Student Visa to pursue on-campus, full-time structured courses or research at educational institutions recognised by the Government of India. Student (S-3) visas cover yoga, Vedic culture, Indian dance, music and Buddhist studies at approved institutions; Student (S-5) visas cover internships.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India

evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals entering India on a Student visa valid for more than 180 days must register with the jurisdictional FRRO or FRO within 14 days of arrival. Pakistani nationals must register within 24 hours. Children under 12 years and OCI cardholders are exempt from registration, and citizens of Nepal and Bhutan are exempt from both visa and registration requirements.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Registration Requirements
evidence.internalNotes: Corroborated by the Study in India Onboarding & FRRO page, which states e-FRRO registration within 14 days of landing. Nationality-dependent rule - never state one universal deadline.

evidence.claimText: Students on an Indian Student visa must not undertake employment or business activity in India, must open a Non-Resident Ordinary (NRO) account with a recognised Indian bank and furnish the details to the FRRO, and must not enrol in off-campus franchise centres, distance-learning study centres of open universities or outreach programmes.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India
evidence.internalNotes: Directly constrains any work-rights or earn-while-you-study claim on India pages. Do not publish part-time work guidance for India.

evidence.claimText: An applicant should possess proof of admission to a full-time regular academic course at a recognised Indian institution and evidence of financial support, and must also hold a No Objection Certificate from the Ministry of Health where the admission is to a medical or paramedical course.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - Onboarding & FRRO
evidence.internalNotes: The portal adds its own disclaimer that document requirements differ across countries and must be confirmed with the nearest Indian embassy.

evidence.claimText: Admission for Foreign Nationals, OCIs, PIOs and NRIs to undergraduate engineering, architecture and planning programmes at NITs, IIEST, IIITs, SPAs and other centrally funded technical institutes runs through the Ministry of Education DASA scheme, and for the 2026-27 year admission is on the basis of JEE (Main) 2026. DASA seats are supernumerary and capped at up to 15 per cent of a programme's total seats. IITs are outside the DASA scheme.
evidence.sourceLabel: Information Brochure DASA 2026 (UG), Central Seat Allocation Board / Ministry of Education
evidence.internalNotes: The qualifying-exam basis has changed between cycles (SAT in earlier cycles, JEE Main for 2026-27). Never state the accepted exam without naming the admission year. Corroborated by dasanit.org, which describes DASA as an MoE scheme for Foreign Nationals, PIOs, OCIs and NRIs to NITs, CFTIs and other premier technical institutions other than IITs.

evidence.claimText: Non-Resident Indians, Overseas Citizens of India and Foreign Nationals are eligible to appear in NEET (UG) and are eligible for admission to medical and dental colleges subject to the rules of the respective State Governments, institutions and the Government of India. Foreign applicants must upload documentary proof of nationality with the application and are directed to confirm eligibility with the competent state and counselling authorities.
evidence.sourceLabel: Information Bulletin NEET (UG)-2026, National Testing Agency
evidence.internalNotes: Chapter 6, sections 1-2. No India medical page may present a NEET-free route. Eligibility is explicitly conditional on state and institution rules, so it varies by college.

evidence.claimText: The National Assessment and Accreditation Council, established in 1994 as an autonomous institution of the UGC, assesses and accredits Indian higher education institutions. The National Institutional Ranking Framework, launched by the Ministry of Education in September 2015, is the government ranking framework for Indian institutions.
evidence.sourceLabel: NAAC - official site
evidence.internalNotes: NIRF corroborated separately at https://www.nirfindia.org/Home (MoE, launched 29 September 2015). Use a NAAC grade or NIRF rank only with the assessment or ranking year stated.

evidence.claimText: The UGC publishes a list of fake universities alongside its lists of Central, State, Deemed-to-be and State Private universities, so institutional recognition must be checked against UGC records before an Indian institution is presented as degree-awarding.
evidence.sourceLabel: University Grants Commission - Higher Education Institutions listings
evidence.internalNotes: Operational rule for this catalogue: no Indian university is published without a verifiable UGC listing and, where applicable, AICTE approval or NMC recognition.

evidence.claimText: India spans Himalayan, tropical coastal, semi-arid and monsoon-affected climate zones, with the southwest monsoon typically running from June to September.
evidence.sourceLabel: India Meteorological Department, Ministry of Earth Sciences
evidence.internalNotes: General climatic framing only; do not present city-level weather claims at country level.
